# CI security policy

The current public-repository lanes add checks; they do not replace the factory's external merge/deep/performance authority. Required status names are enabled only after actual hosted acceptance. CODEOWNERS requests Nick's review; native rules must require that review to enforce it. Nick's explicitly adopted exception is owner authority, not independent review by a second person.

PR code runs on fresh standard hosted machines with no secrets, release token, cloud identity or signing key. There is no privileged PR artifact consumer and no PR cache in a release path. All action references and downloaded CI executables are pinned. Dependabot proposes Cargo and action updates without auto-merge. Scanner policy changes need code-owner review. No advisory or license exception is included. The checked-in secret-fixtures.json contains exact, independently reviewed false-positive dispositions for static public test data; it grants no exception for operational credentials.

Gitleaks scans the complete tracked source, ignoring user configurations and inline suppression directives; matches are reported as counts and source locations, never matched values. Only a single line matching its reviewed path, line number, generic rule and full line SHA256 can be classified as a known synthetic fixture; new, changed, multiline and differently located matches fail. No directory-wide test exclusion or inline allow marker is honored. Workflow syntax is checked by actionlint (ShellCheck is not supplied by this lane). The explicit linter-only Ubuntu26 label list compensates for actionlint1.7.12 lag; the labels were confirmed in the official actions/runner-images catalogue. It does not create self-hosted runners. Cargo-deny checks advisories, declared license allowlist, duplicate versions and source restrictions; duplicate versions remain warnings. The wildcard lint is deliberately omitted: the product uses unversioned local workspace paths, and cargo-deny0.20.2 misresolves inherited path declarations. Locked fetch still binds all resolved package versions; unknown registry/Git sources remain denied. Known vulnerable dependencies, unlicensed/disallowed dependencies and unknown Git/registry sources fail. A policy failure is not automatically waived because it came from an existing dependency. Missing database/parser/execution results fail.

CodeQL analyzes Rust and GitHub Actions without a source build. Analysis/upload success alone is not the alert gate: the result policy reads SARIF and blocks high/critical security-severity scores (>=7), unscored error-level results and analyzer errors. Missing results, empty query rule inventories or unknown result rules refuse. The hosted CodeQL analyze step must succeed; this parser does not infer completed query coverage from an absent invocation record or zero alerts. Lower-severity results remain visible in GitHub code scanning for triage. CodeQL no-build analysis has generated-code limitations. Secret scanning/push protection and native code-scanning merge rules are settings whose actual activation/readback are separate.

The fast gate prefetches with `--locked`, switches Cargo children offline, and refuses changes to tracked source content, modes and symlink targets, Cargo.lock or the benchmark baseline. It runs no performance workload and never rebaselines. Native macOS ARM QA covers case-insensitive filesystem tests missing on Linux; Linux ARM source QA does not promise an ARM release archive. The Windows Server hosted lane checks only model/schema/graph and is not a Windows11 or full-product qualification claim.

Coverage remains advisory. Its failure is visible and does not change the result of required tests. Seven-day retention bounds diagnostic artifacts. The required aggregates reject failed, cancelled and skipped dependencies. PR supersession may cancel read-only work; release publication has a separate concurrency policy.

## Release/installer integration interfaces

- `python3 scripts/ci/run_fast.py`: non-root Linux/macOS fast correctness, fetch locked then offline; return0 only on gate success and unchanged tracked source/lockfile/baseline. Requires Rust from rust-toolchain.toml, Node, git and native test prerequisites.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/ci -v`: CI policy unit/boundary tests. The same job runs tests/release and tests/installer under Python3.13.
- `python3 scripts/ci/check_sarif.py DIRECTORY`: CodeQL result gate; returns nonzero on blocking or incomplete results. This is not proof that CodeQL ran on a particular source revision; hosted run identity supplies that binding.
- `python3 scripts/ci/install_tools.py --out EMPTY_DIRECTORY TOOL...`: exact tools from the reviewed tools.json manifest. No downloaded executable is run before digest validation.

No new security report is a release signature. The existing founder-held FIDO checksum signature remains outside CI; publication must validate it against exact candidate bytes.
